title: Troubleshooting
text:
The package fails in one of three ways: it raises before sending anything, it raises because Umami answered with an error, or it returns normally and nothing shows up in the dashboard. This page covers each in turn and ends with the order to check things in.

Read the exception first



Exception
Raised when
Where to look




umami.errors.OperationNotAllowedError
Required setup is missing: no set_url_base(), or a query call before login(). No request was made.
Setup errors


umami.errors.ValidationError
An argument is wrong: blank event name, missing hostname or website id, negative revenue. No request was made.
Validation errors


httpx2.HTTPStatusError
Umami answered with a non-2xx status. The request was made.
HTTP errors


httpx2.ConnectError, httpx2.ReadTimeout and other httpx2.TransportError subclasses
The server could not be reached or did not answer in time.
HTTP errors



OperationNotAllowedError subclasses ValidationError, so one except umami.errors.ValidationError catches both. verify_token() and heartbeat() never raise; they return False instead.


Setup errors

Set a URL base with set_url_base() or call set_cloud_api_key().

Nothing has been configured yet. Call set_url_base('https://your-instance') for self-hosted, or set_cloud_api_key(key) for Cloud, before anything else. If you configured it in one module and the error comes from another, check that both run in the same process and that the configuration code ran first.

Call login() or set_cloud_api_key() before proceeding.

You called websites(), website_stats(), or active_users() without a credential. These need login() on self-hosted or a Cloud key. Sending events does not.

login() is not used in Cloud mode; your API key from set_cloud_api_key() is the credential.

A Cloud key is set, so there is nothing to log in to. Remove the login() call, or call clear_cloud_api_key() first if you meant to talk to a self-hosted instance.




Validation errors
Each message names the argument to fix:

URL must not be empty. and The url must start with the HTTP scheme (http:// or https://). come from set_url_base(). Pass the full instance URL including the scheme.
The hostname must be set, either as a parameter here or via set_hostname(). and The website_id must be set, either as a parameter here or via set_website_id(). come from the send functions. Set the defaults once at startup or pass the argument on the call.
The event_name is required. means the name was empty or whitespace.
distinct_id must be a string or integer. means you passed a bool, float, list, or other type.
Revenue must be a number (int or float)., Revenue must be >= 0., and Currency must be a non-empty string. come from new_revenue_event().
API key must not be empty. and region must be 'us', 'eu', or None. come from set_cloud_api_key().
Username cannot be empty and Password cannot be empty come from login().



Login and token problems
login() raises httpx2.HTTPStatusError with a 401 when the username or password is wrong. Check the credentials against the Umami login page.
A query call that worked earlier and now raises a 401 means the token expired. Umami tokens are temporary. Call login() again, or check first with verify_token(), which returns False for an expired token without raising.
verify_token() returning False right after a successful login() usually means the server is unreachable, not that the token is bad. Check heartbeat().
On Cloud, a 401 or 403 means the API key is wrong, revoked, or used on a route the Cloud API does not allow for keys. Create a new key in the Cloud dashboard and try again.


HTTP errors
Inspect the status code and body before guessing:
import httpx2

try:
    umami.websites()
except httpx2.HTTPStatusError as e:
    print(e.response.status_code, e.response.text)

404 on every call: url_base is wrong. The most common mistake is including /api, which produces /api/api/websites. Pass the instance root only. A 404 can also mean the host serves something other than Umami.
401: see Login and token problems.
405: your Umami version does not accept the HTTP method the package used. Upgrade the package; versions before 0.6.25 used POST for the heartbeat.
429 on Cloud: you exceeded the documented limit of 50 calls per 15 seconds. Pace your calls; the package does not retry.
5xx: the Umami server has a problem. Check its logs.
ConnectError: the host name does not resolve, the port is closed, or you used http:// where the server only speaks https://.
ReadTimeout: Umami did not answer within the default five second httpx2 timeout. The package does not expose a timeout setting; check the server’s load.



Event sent but nothing appears
The call returned a dict and raised nothing, but the dashboard shows no event. Work through these in order.

The return value is {}. Tracking is disabled. Something called umami.disable(), usually a test or development setting. Call umami.enable() or check the condition that disables it. A real response contains keys such as cache.
Umami’s bot filter dropped the request. Umami rejects requests whose User-Agent looks like a bot, and it may still answer 200. The package sends a desktop Chrome user agent by default, so this only happens when you pass your own ua to new_page_view(). Use a browser user agent, or set DISABLE_BOT_CHECK=true in the Umami server’s environment. That variable is read by the Umami server, not by this package.
Wrong website id. The event was recorded against another website. Compare the id you set with the one in the dashboard URL, and remember that an explicit website_id argument wins over set_website_id().
Wrong mode. A Cloud key is set, so the event went to Umami Cloud rather than your self-hosted instance, or the other way round. clear_cloud_api_key() switches back to self-hosted.
Dashboard range or timezone. Events appear under the date range selected in the dashboard, in the dashboard’s timezone. Widen the range and refresh.
It is in the Events list, not the Pages list. Custom events appear in the Events section at the bottom of the website page. Page views appear in Pages. Revenue appears in the Revenue report once Umami has processed the revenue and currency properties.



heartbeat() returns False
heartbeat() returns False for any failure, including configuration problems, so it does not tell you which one you have:

set_url_base() or set_cloud_api_key() has not been called.
The server is down or unreachable from this machine.
url_base points at the wrong host or includes /api.
On Cloud, the API key is invalid. Cloud has no heartbeat endpoint, so the package calls the authenticated /me endpoint instead.

Call umami.websites() or another raising function to see the real exception.


Queries return wrong numbers

active_users() always returns 0, or website_stats() ignores the url and host filters: you are on a package version older than 0.6.25. Upgrade.
website_stats() numbers do not match the dashboard for the same days: the dashboard uses its own timezone and your datetime values are naive and interpreted in the local timezone of the process. Pass timezone-aware datetimes.



Fix order
Fix configuration first, because ValidationError and OperationNotAllowedError are raised before any request and nothing else can work until they stop. Then confirm connectivity with heartbeat(), then the credential with verify_token(), and only then look at the event itself.
If you find a problem the package should handle better, open an issue at https://github.com/mikeckennedy/umami-python/issues.

title: Sending events
text:
Three functions send data to Umami: new_event() for custom events, new_page_view() for page views, and new_revenue_event() for events that carry a monetary amount. Each has an _async twin with the same signature and the same return value. None of them require a login. They need set_url_base() (or set_cloud_api_key()), a website id, and a hostname.
All three share a few arguments:








Argument
Default
Notes




hostname
value from set_hostname()
The domain visitors see. Required one way or the other.


website_id
value from set_website_id()
Required one way or the other.


url
'/' for events, required for page views
The page path the event is attributed to.


referrer
''
Shown in the Referrers section when set.


language
'en-US'
Recorded on the session.


screen
'1920x1080'
Recorded on the session.


ip_address
not sent
Sent as ip when non-blank, so Umami geolocates the real visitor instead of your server.


distinct_id
not sent
A stable per-user id. See below.



Missing hostname or website_id raises umami.errors.ValidationError before any request is made.

Custom events
umami.new_event(
    event_name='checkout-completed',
    url='/checkout',
    title='Checkout',            # defaults to event_name
    custom_data={'plan': 'pro', 'seats': 3},
    referrer='https://news.ycombinator.com',
)
event_name is required and must not be blank. title is the page title Umami records alongside the event and defaults to the event name. custom_data becomes the event’s properties; it is not shown in the main dashboard view but is available by clicking into the event and through the Umami API.


Page views
A page view is what the browser tracker records when a page loads. Send one from the server when you render a page for a client that cannot run JavaScript, or when you serve content outside the browser.
umami.new_page_view(page_title='Account details', url='/account/details', ip_address=request.client.host)
page_title and url are both required. Page views have no event name and no custom data.
new_page_view() accepts one extra argument the others do not: ua, the user agent recorded for the visitor. It defaults to a desktop Chrome user agent because Umami drops requests whose user agent looks like a bot. Pass the real browser’s user agent when you have it so the Browsers and Devices sections stay accurate. new_event() has no ua argument.


Revenue
new_revenue_event() is new_event() with two keys added to custom_data: revenue and currency. Umami’s revenue report reads those keys.
umami.new_revenue_event(
    revenue=19.99,
    currency='USD',              # ISO 4217, defaults to 'USD'
    event_name='checkout-cart',  # defaults to 'revenue'
    url='/checkout',
    custom_data={'product': 'widget', 'quantity': 2},
)
Validation before the request: revenue must be an int or float greater than or equal to zero, and currency must be non-blank. If your custom_data already has revenue or currency keys they are overwritten by the arguments.


Per-user attribution with distinct_id
Pass distinct_id on any of the three functions to attach a stable identifier for the logged-in user. It is sent as the payload field id, which Umami uses to tie sessions and events to one visitor across devices.
umami.new_event(event_name='login', distinct_id=user.id)
Rules the package enforces:

str and int are accepted. Integers are sent as strings.
Blank or whitespace-only strings are ignored and no id is sent.
bool and any other type raise ValidationError. The bool check is explicit because True is an int in Python.

Use an internal user id or a hash, not an email address or other raw personal data.


What gets sent
Every call makes one POST to /api/send with a body like this. There is no batching and no retry.
{
  "type": "event",
  "payload": {
    "website": "978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60",
    "hostname": "example.com",
    "url": "/checkout",
    "title": "checkout-cart",
    "name": "checkout-cart",
    "data": {"product": "widget", "quantity": 2, "revenue": 19.99, "currency": "USD"},
    "referrer": "",
    "language": "en-US",
    "screen": "1920x1080",
    "id": "user-42"
  }
}
A page view is the same shape without name and data. The ip field is present only when you pass ip_address, and id only when you pass distinct_id.


Return values
The functions return the parsed JSON response from Umami as a dict. When tracking has been turned off with disable() they validate their arguments and return {} without making a request. A non-2xx response raises httpx2.HTTPStatusError.


Async
Each function has an _async twin that sends the same payload and returns the same value.
await umami.new_event_async(event_name='checkout-completed', url='/checkout')
await umami.new_page_view_async(page_title='Home', url='/')
await umami.new_revenue_event_async(revenue=19.99, url='/checkout')
The configuration functions are synchronous only. Call set_url_base() and friends once at startup, before your event loop starts handling requests.
If an event does not appear in the dashboard, see Troubleshooting.

title: User Guide
text:
Umami records page views and custom events from a small JavaScript tracker in your pages. That works for clicks and form submits, but some of the events you care about most never happen in the browser. A purchase that completes inside a payment webhook, a background job that finishes, or an API call from a mobile app all happen in your Python code, with no HTML element to attach a data-umami-event attribute to.
umami-analytics is a Python client for the parts of the Umami API that a backend needs. It sends custom events, page views, and revenue to a self-hosted Umami instance or to Umami Cloud, and it reads back the basic numbers: your websites, page views and visitors over a date range, and the number of active visitors right now. Every network call has a synchronous function and an _async twin.
The package is deliberately a partial wrapper. It covers configuration, authentication, sending events, listing websites, summary stats, and active users. Reports, sessions, event data, and the rest of the Umami API are one HTTP call away with the token the package already holds, and the How it works page shows how.

Where to go next

Getting started: install the package, point it at your instance, send your first event, and see where it lands in the dashboard.
Sending events: custom events, page views, revenue, custom data, and per-user distinct_id.
Authentication: self-hosted login versus an Umami Cloud API key, and when a login is actually required.
Querying stats: listing websites, page views and visitors for a date range, filters, and active users.
Troubleshooting: what each error means and what to do about it, including events that return 200 but never appear.
Testing and CI: keep test runs out of your analytics with disable(), and mock the HTTP boundary.
Configuration: every setting, its default, and which calls need it.
How it works: module-global state, request routing, headers, user agents, and what the package does not do.
FAQ: short answers to the questions that come up most.

The API Reference documents every public function and model, with the sync and async twins side by side.

title: Getting started
text:
This page takes you from an empty environment to a custom event in your Umami dashboard. It assumes you have a running Umami instance (self-hosted or Umami Cloud) and a website registered in it. If you are on Umami Cloud, read the Cloud section at the end before the configuration step.

Install
The package on PyPI is umami-analytics. The import name is umami.
uv add umami-analytics
# or
pip install umami-analytics
Do not run pip install umami. That is an unrelated package with the same import name.
The package supports Python 3.10 and newer and depends on httpx2 and pydantic.


Configure
Everything is a module-level function. There is no client object to create. Configure the module once when your application starts, and every later call uses that state.
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')  # your instance root, without /api
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')
Three things to know about these calls:

set_url_base() is required before anything else. It validates that the URL starts with http:// or https:// and strips a trailing slash. Do not include /api; the package adds the endpoint paths itself.
set_website_id() takes the website id from the Umami dashboard (Settings, Websites, Edit). It becomes the default for every later call, and any call can override it with its own website_id argument.
set_hostname() is the hostname recorded on each event. Umami uses it to group traffic, so use the domain visitors see, not the hostname of the server sending the event.

You do not need to log in to send events. Login is only required for the query functions, and the Authentication page covers it.


Send your first event
response = umami.new_event(
    event_name='purchase-course',
    url='/courses/python-for-absolute-beginners',
    custom_data={'plan': 'individual', 'price': 69},
)
event_name is the only required argument. The url defaults to / and is the page path the event is attributed to. custom_data is any JSON-serializable dict; Umami stores it as event properties.
If this call returns without raising, Umami accepted the event.


Read the result
Open your website in the Umami dashboard. The event appears in two places:

In the Events section at the bottom of the website page, listed under its event_name with a count.
In the Pages section, as traffic on the url you passed.

Click the event name to see the properties from custom_data.
The return value is the JSON body Umami sent back, parsed into a dict. On current Umami versions it contains a cache token plus sessionId and visitId. You can ignore it. The exact keys depend on the Umami server version, and the package does not use them.
If the call raised an exception, or returned normally but nothing shows up, go to Troubleshooting. The most common cause of a silent miss is Umami’s bot filter rejecting the request, and the page explains how to tell.


Check the connection
heartbeat() tells you whether the configured instance is reachable. It never raises; it returns False on any problem, including a missing set_url_base().
if not umami.heartbeat():
    print('Umami is not reachable')


Umami Cloud
On Umami Cloud you authenticate with an API key instead of a URL and a login. Create a key in the Cloud dashboard, then replace set_url_base() with set_cloud_api_key():
import umami

umami.set_cloud_api_key('your-cloud-api-key')  # region='us' or 'eu' is optional
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')

umami.new_event(event_name='purchase-course', url='/courses/python-for-absolute-beginners')
Events go to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send and query calls go to https://api.umami.is/v1, with the key sent as an x-umami-api-key header. Do not call login() in Cloud mode; it raises OperationNotAllowedError. See Authentication for the details of both modes and how to switch between them.


Next steps

Sending events covers page views, revenue, and the per-user distinct_id.
Testing and CI shows how to keep your test suite from writing to your real analytics.
Querying stats reads the numbers back out.

title: Configuration
text:
All configuration is module-global state set by plain function calls. There is no configuration file, no environment variable, and no client object. Set things once at startup; every later call reads them.

Settings









Function
Sets
Default
Required by




set_url_base(url)
The instance root for self-hosted mode. Must start with http:// or https://. A trailing slash is removed. /api must not be included.
none
Every call in self-hosted mode


set_website_id(website_id)
Default website for sending and querying.
none
Send functions, website_stats(), active_users() unless passed per call


set_hostname(hostname)
Default hostname recorded on events and page views.
none
Send functions unless passed per call


set_cloud_api_key(key, region=None)
Umami Cloud key and optional 'us' or 'eu' region. Switches to Cloud mode.
none
Every call in Cloud mode


clear_cloud_api_key()
Removes the key and region. Back to self-hosted mode.

Stores the token for query calls. Self-hosted only.
none
websites(), website_stats(), active_users(), verify_token()


enable() / disable()
Whether the send functions make requests.
enabled




The setters are synchronous only. There is no set_url_base_async().

What happens on a second call

set_url_base() again replaces the previous value.
login() again replaces the stored token. There is no logout.
set_cloud_api_key() again replaces the key and region.
set_cloud_api_key() after login() switches to Cloud mode. The login token is kept but unused until clear_cloud_api_key().
set_url_base() while a Cloud key is set stores the URL but it is ignored until clear_cloud_api_key().
clear_cloud_api_key() when no key is set does nothing.
enable() and disable() are idempotent.



Precedence
An explicit website_id or hostname argument on a call always wins over the value set with set_website_id() or set_hostname(). Passing None falls back to the default; passing an empty string is treated as missing and raises ValidationError.


Reading the current state
The public API has no getters. is_logged_in() tells you whether a token or Cloud key is present. For anything else, keep your own record of what you configured. The module umami.impl holds the values as plain attributes (url_base, default_website_id, default_hostname, auth_token, api_key, cloud_region, tracking_enabled), which is useful in a debugger and in tests, but it is an implementation detail rather than a supported interface.


Version
umami.__version__ is read from the installed distribution metadata and is '0.0.0' when the package is imported from a source checkout that was not installed. umami.user_agent is the User-Agent sent on query calls and includes the version and Python version.

# umami-analytics

Umami's browser tracker cannot see events that happen inside server code, such as a purchase completed by a webhook. `umami-analytics` sends those as Umami custom events, page views, or revenue, and reads back basic stats. It is a module of functions with module-global configuration; there is no client class, no CLI, and it reads no environment variables. Bad arguments raise `umami.errors.ValidationError`, missing setup raises `umami.errors.OperationNotAllowedError`, and non-2xx responses raise `httpx2.HTTPStatusError`.

## Install

```bash
uv add umami-analytics   # or: pip install umami-analytics   (import name is `umami`; never `pip install umami`)
```

## Use

```python
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')  # must be first; instance root, no /api
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')  # the domain visitors see

umami.new_event(event_name='purchase-course', url='/courses/python', custom_data={'plan': 'pro'})
umami.new_revenue_event(revenue=19.99, currency='USD', event_name='checkout', url='/checkout', distinct_id=user.id)
await umami.new_event_async(event_name='signup')  # every network call has an _async twin
```

In tests or local development, after the setters: `umami.disable()`. The send functions then validate and return `{}` with no request. In CI, select that with your own setting, for example `if os.environ.get('APP_ENV') != 'production': umami.disable()`.

For Umami Cloud, replace `set_url_base()` with `umami.set_cloud_api_key(key, region=None)`; never call `login()` in Cloud mode.

## Rules

- `set_url_base()` or `set_cloud_api_key()` must run before any other call, including `heartbeat()`. Setters are sync only and not thread-safe; call them once at startup.
- Sending events needs no login. `websites()`, `website_stats()`, `active_users()`, and `verify_token()` need `login()` (self-hosted) or a Cloud key.
- The two modes are exclusive. A Cloud key wins over `set_url_base()`; `login()` raises `OperationNotAllowedError` while a key is set; `clear_cloud_api_key()` switches back and keeps any earlier login token.
- `login()` tokens expire. `verify_token()` returns `False` instead of raising; log in again when it does. `login()` twice replaces the token; there is no logout.
- `disable()` silences only the three send functions. Query and auth functions always hit the network. A forgotten `disable()` in production is silent: calls return `{}`.
- `hostname` and `website_id` must come from the setters or the call, or `ValidationError` is raised before any request. Empty strings count as missing. An explicit argument beats the setter.
- `event_name` is required and non-blank for `new_event()`. `new_page_view()` requires `page_title` and `url` and has no `event_name` or `custom_data`. `url` defaults to `'/'` on events and is required on page views.
- `distinct_id` accepts `str` or `int` and is sent as payload `id`. Blank strings are dropped. `bool` and other types raise `ValidationError`.
- `new_revenue_event()` requires `revenue >= 0` as `int` or `float` and a non-blank `currency` (default `'USD'`); it overwrites `revenue` and `currency` keys in `custom_data`.
- Only `new_page_view()` accepts `ua`. Passing `ua` to `new_event()` is a `TypeError`. The default is a Chrome user agent because Umami drops bot-like user agents, often while still returning 200.
- `website_stats()` takes `datetime` objects and converts them with `timestamp()`, so naive datetimes mean local time. Its `url` and `host` filters are sent as `path` and `hostname`. `websites()` returns only the first page.
- One HTTP request per call, five second timeout, no retry, no batching, no connection pool. `heartbeat()` and `verify_token()` never raise.
- `umami.models` are Pydantic models (`Website`, `WebsiteStats`, `LoginResponse`). `OperationNotAllowedError` subclasses `ValidationError`.

## Decision table

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Self-hosted instance | `set_url_base(url)`, then `login(user, pw)` only if you will query |
| Umami Cloud | `set_cloud_api_key(key, region='us' or 'eu' or None)`; no `set_url_base()`, no `login()` |
| Record a business event | `new_event(event_name, url=..., custom_data={...})` |
| Record money | `new_revenue_event(revenue, currency='USD', event_name=..., url=...)` |
| Record a server-rendered page load | `new_page_view(page_title, url, ua=request_user_agent, ip_address=client_ip)` |
| Tie events to a logged-in user | `distinct_id=user.id` on any send call |
| Silence analytics in tests or dev | `umami.disable()` after the setters |
| Check the token still works | `verify_token()`; `check_server=False` for a local presence check |
| Check the server is up | `heartbeat()` |
| Visitors, views, bounces for a range | `website_stats(start_at, end_at, website_id=None, url=..., country=...)` |
| Visitors on the site right now | `active_users(website_id=None)` |
| Anything else in the Umami API | Call it with `httpx2` using `login().token` or the Cloud key |

## API

- `set_url_base(url) -> None`: raises `ValidationError` unless `url` starts with `http://` or `https://`; strips a trailing slash.
- `set_website_id(website_id) -> None`, `set_hostname(hostname) -> None`: defaults for later calls; not validated until a send.
- `set_cloud_api_key(key, region=None) -> None`: raises `ValidationError` on a blank key or a region other than `'us'`, `'eu'`, `None`. `clear_cloud_api_key() -> None`.
- `enable() -> None`, `disable() -> None`: toggle the send functions. `is_logged_in() -> bool`: token or key present, no network.
- `login(username, password) -> models.LoginResponse` / `login_async`: raises `OperationNotAllowedError` in Cloud mode or without `set_url_base()`, `ValidationError` on empty fields, `HTTPStatusError` on bad credentials.
- `verify_token(check_server=True) -> bool` / `verify_token_async`: never raises.
- `new_event(event_name, hostname=None, url='/', website_id=None, title=None, custom_data=None, referrer='', language='en-US', screen='1920x1080', ip_address=None, distinct_id=None) -> dict` / `new_event_async`: `{}` when disabled.
- `new_revenue_event(revenue, currency='USD', event_name='revenue', ...same as new_event...) -> dict` / `new_revenue_event_async`.
- `new_page_view(page_title, url, hostname=None, website_id=None, referrer='', language='en-US', screen='1920x1080', ua=<chrome>, ip_address=None, distinct_id=None) -> dict` / `new_page_view_async`.
- `websites() -> list[models.Website]` / `websites_async`: `Website.id` is the website id; `user` or `createUser` may be `None`.
- `website_stats(start_at, end_at, website_id=None, url=None, referrer=None, title=None, query=None, event=None, host=None, os=None, browser=None, device=None, country=None, region=None, city=None) -> models.WebsiteStats` / `website_stats_async`: fields `pageviews`, `visitors`, `visits`, `bounces`, `totaltime`, optional `comparison`.
- `active_users(website_id=None) -> int` / `active_users_async`.
- `heartbeat() -> bool` / `heartbeat_async`: `False` on any failure, including missing configuration.

## What a send looks like

`new_revenue_event(revenue=19.99, event_name='checkout', url='/checkout', custom_data={'plan': 'pro'}, distinct_id=42)` makes one `POST` to `{url_base}/api/send` with:

```json
{"type": "event",
 "payload": {"website": "978435e2-...", "hostname": "example.com", "url": "/checkout",
             "title": "checkout", "name": "checkout",
             "data": {"plan": "pro", "revenue": 19.99, "currency": "USD"},
             "referrer": "", "language": "en-US", "screen": "1920x1080", "id": "42"}}
```

The return value is Umami's JSON, typically `{"cache": "...", "sessionId": "...", "visitId": "..."}`, or `{}` when disabled. In the dashboard the event appears under Events as `checkout`, the page under Pages as `/checkout`, and the amount in the Revenue report. If nothing appears, fix in this order: configuration (the `ValidationError` and `OperationNotAllowedError` messages name the missing piece), then `heartbeat()`, then `verify_token()`, then the bot filter (custom `ua`), website id, mode, and dashboard date range.

title: verify_token()
text:
Verify that the currently stored credential is still valid.


Usage
Source


verify_token(check_server=True)


In self-hosted/token mode this checks the auth token obtained from login(); in Cloud mode it checks the API key set via set_cloud_api_key(). Tokens issued by login() are temporary and eventually expire, after which you must log in again.
This function never raises: any error (network failure, missing credential, expired or rejected token, non-2xx response) results in a return value of False.


Parameters


check_server: bool = True

If True (default), contact the server to confirm the credential is valid — self-hosted posts to /api/auth/verify, while Cloud mode fetches /api/me. If False, perform only a local check (equivalent to is_logged_in()) with no network request.





Returns


 bool

True if the credential is valid (or, when check_server is False, simply
present), False otherwise.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
if not umami.verify_token():
    umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')  # token expired

Usage

set_url_base(url)


Required before any self-hosted operation (login, sending events, or querying stats). Provide the root URL of your instance without the trailing ‘/api’, for example ‘https://analytics.example.com’. A trailing slash is stripped automatically. Use this together with login() for self-hosted/token mode; do not combine it with set_cloud_api_key(), which selects Umami Cloud mode instead.


Parameters


url: str

The base URL of your instance, without ‘/api’. Must start with ‘http://’ or ‘https://’.





Raises


 ValidationError

If url is empty or whitespace-only, or if it does not start with ‘http://’ or ‘https://’.

import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://analytics.example.com')

title: set_cloud_api_key()
text:
Authenticate against Umami Cloud with an API key instead of login().


Usage
Source


set_cloud_api_key(key, region=None)


Enables “Cloud mode”: data and management calls are routed to https://api.umami.is/v1 and authenticated with the ‘x-umami-api-key’ header, and events are sent to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send. You do not need to call set_url_base() or login() in this mode; Cloud mode and self-hosted/token mode are mutually exclusive. Call clear_cloud_api_key() to exit Cloud mode and return to self-hosted/token behavior.


Parameters


key: str

Your Umami Cloud API key.

region: Optional[str] = None

Optional ‘us’ or ‘eu’ to pin the data region. Defaults to the region of the account that owns the key.





Raises


 ValidationError

If key is empty or whitespace-only, or if region is provided but is not ‘us’ or ‘eu’.





Example
import umami

umami.set_cloud_api_key('your-cloud-api-key', region='us')
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')

title: new_revenue_event()
text:
Create a new revenue event in Umami. This is a convenience wrapper around


Usage
Source


new_revenue_event(
    revenue,
    currency="USD",
    event_name="revenue",
    hostname=None,
    url="/",
    website_id=None,
    title=None,
    custom_data=None,
    referrer="",
    language="en-US",
    screen="1920x1080",
    ip_address=None,
    distinct_id=None
)


new_event() that automatically includes the revenue and currency properties required by Umami’s revenue tracking.
Requires set_url_base() (or set_cloud_api_key() for Cloud mode) and a website_id and hostname, either set globally via set_website_id()/set_hostname() or passed here. Login is not required to send events. If tracking has been turned off with disable(), the inputs are still validated but no HTTP request is made and an empty dict is returned.


Parameters


revenue: float

The monetary amount of the transaction. Must be a number (int or float) >= 0.

currency: str = "USD"

ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. ‘USD’, ‘EUR’). Must be non-empty. Defaults to ‘USD’.

event_name: str = "revenue"

The name of your custom event. Defaults to ‘revenue’.

hostname: Optional[str] = None

Optional hostname identifying the client (e.g. ‘example.com’); overrides the set_hostname() value.

url: str = "/"

The URL associated with the event (e.g. ‘/checkout’). Defaults to ‘/’.

website_id: Optional[str] = None

Optional Umami website ID; overrides the set_website_id() value.

title: Optional[str] = None

The display title of the event. Defaults to event_name when omitted.

custom_data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

Additional key/value data sent with the event. The ‘revenue’ and ‘currency’ keys are overwritten by the values above.

referrer: str = ""

The referrer of the client, if any. Defaults to ’’.

language: str = "en-US"

The language of the event/client. Defaults to ‘en-US’.

screen: str = "1920x1080"

The screen resolution of the client. Defaults to ‘1920x1080’.

ip_address: Optional[str] = None

Optional true IP address of the user, useful when sending events from server-side request handlers.

distinct_id: Optional[Union[str, int]] = None

Optional Umami distinct ID for the user, as a string or integer, sent to the API as the payload field ‘id’. Blank or whitespace-only values are ignored (no id is sent).





Returns


 dict

The parsed JSON response from the Umami API as a dict, or an empty dict
if tracking is disabled.





Raises


 ValidationError

If revenue is not a number, revenue is negative, currency or event_name is blank, distinct_id is an invalid type, or hostname or website_id is not set (here or via set_hostname()/set_website_id()).

 OperationNotAllowedError

If neither set_url_base() nor set_cloud_api_key() has been called.

 httpx.HTTPStatusError

If the Umami API returns a non-2xx response.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')
umami.new_revenue_event(
    revenue=19.99,
    currency='USD',
    event_name='checkout-cart',
    url='/checkout',
)

title: login_async()
text:
Log into a self-hosted Umami instance and retrieve a temporary auth token.


Usage
Source


login_async(username, password)


On success, the returned token is stored internally and used to authenticate subsequent data calls (websites_async(), website_stats_async(), active_users_async(), verify_token_async()). Tokens expire, so you may need to log in again; check validity with verify_token_async().
Requires set_url_base() to have been called first. This is the self-hosted/token authentication path and is not used in Cloud mode; in Cloud mode call set_cloud_api_key() instead.


Parameters


username: str

Your Umami username.

password: str

Your Umami password.





Returns


 models.LoginResponse

A models.LoginResponse containing the auth token and the logged-in
user’s details. You do not need to store this yourself; the token is
retained internally.





Raises


 OperationNotAllowedError

If Cloud mode is active (set_cloud_api_key() was called), or if set_url_base() has not been called.

 ValidationError

If username or password is empty.

 httpx.HTTPStatusError

If the server returns a non-2xx response, e.g. on invalid credentials.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
login = await umami.login_async('admin', 'super-secret')

text:
Whether a credential is currently set locally.


Usage
Source


is_logged_in()


Returns


 bool

True if a self-hosted login token (set by login()) or an Umami Cloud
API key (set by set_cloud_api_key()) is present, False otherwise. This
only reflects that a credential exists in this process, not that it is
still valid on the server — use verify_token() to confirm validity.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
umami.is_logged_in()  # False
umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
umami.is_logged_in()  # True

title: heartbeat_async()
text:
Check whether the configured Umami server is reachable and healthy.


Usage
Source


heartbeat_async()


In self-hosted mode this issues a GET to {url_base}/api/heartbeat. In Cloud mode (after set_cloud_api_key()), Umami Cloud has no /api/heartbeat endpoint, so this performs an authenticated GET on the /me endpoint as a liveness check instead.
Requires set_url_base() (self-hosted) or set_cloud_api_key() (Cloud) to have been called first; login() is not required. This function never raises: any failure (missing configuration, connection error, or a non-2xx response) is caught and reported as False.


Returns


 bool

True if the server is reachable and responded successfully; False on
any error, including when no url_base or Cloud API key has been
configured.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
if not await umami.heartbeat_async():
    print('Umami is unavailable')

title: errors.ValidationError
text:
Base exception raised when an input or argument fails validation.


Usage
Source


errors.ValidationError()


The SDK raises this (or its subclass OperationNotAllowedError) for invalid or malformed inputs before any network request is made. Examples include an empty or non-HTTP url_base, an invalid distinct_id, a negative or non-numeric revenue amount, an empty currency, empty login credentials, and an invalid Cloud API key or region.
Because OperationNotAllowedError subclasses this type, catching ValidationError also catches missing-state errors.


Example
import umami

try:
    umami.new_revenue_event(revenue=-1)
except umami.errors.ValidationError as e:
    print(e)  # Revenue must be >= 0.

title: enable()
text:
Enable event and page view tracking.


Usage
Source


enable()


When enabled, the send functions new_event(), new_revenue_event(), and new_page_view() send data to Umami normally. This is the default state.
Only the send functions are affected; query and authentication functions (such as login(), websites(), website_stats(), active_users(), verify_token(), and heartbeat()) always run regardless of this setting. Call disable() to turn tracking off.


Example
import umami

umami.disable()  # e.g. while running tests
umami.enable()   # back to sending events

title: clear_cloud_api_key()
text:
Exit Cloud mode and return to self-hosted/token behavior.


Usage
Source


clear_cloud_api_key()


Clears the API key and region set by set_cloud_api_key(). After calling this, self-hosted operations again require set_url_base() and login(). A token from an earlier login() is kept, so if you logged in before switching to Cloud mode you do not need to log in again.


Example
import umami

umami.set_cloud_api_key('your-cloud-api-key')
# ... later, go back to a self-hosted instance:
umami.clear_cloud_api_key()
umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')

Usage

active_users(website_id=None)


Requires authentication: call login() (self-hosted) or set_cloud_api_key() (Umami Cloud) first.


Parameters


website_id: Optional[str] = None

OPTIONAL: The value of your website_id in Umami (overrides the set_website_id() value).





Returns


 int

The count of visitors currently active on the website.





Raises


 OperationNotAllowedError

Added

pydantic.Field(description=...) metadata on every response-model field, plus a griffe-pydantic dev dependency, enriching the response models for IDEs, JSON schema, and future API-reference rendering. Note: the current Great Docs version (0.13.0) does not load griffe extensions, so the rendered field docs still come from the docstring Attributes: sections; the Field descriptions will surface on the docs site once the generator loads the extension.



Changed

Synchronous send functions now return the Umami API’s JSON response as a dict (and {} when tracking is disabled), matching their async twins. Previously new_event(), new_revenue_event(), and new_page_view() returned None; new_page_view_async() also now returns the response dict instead of None.
Missing or blank required event fields (hostname, website_id, event_name) now raise umami.errors.ValidationError instead of a bare Exception, so they can be caught alongside the SDK’s other validation errors.
Website.shareId, Website.resetAt, and Website.deletedAt are now optional (default None), so a websites response that omits those keys no longer raises pydantic.ValidationError.
README now points to the new documentation site at https://mkennedy.codes/docs/umami-python/ (added status badges, a documentation pointer near the top, and a “Documentation” section linking the full API reference). Docs-only change — no code or packaging changes.
Docstrings across the public API were expanded and corrected for the generated documentation site (Great Docs renders them verbatim, and they feed llms.txt). Added Raises: sections to every raising function; fixed website_stats() / website_stats_async() to document their real return type (models.WebsiteStats, not the nonexistent WebsiteStatsResponse); removed unprofessional/inaccurate prose from verify_token (the “minutes, hours, or years” hedge) and new_event (the “not sure how this is different” aside); corrected new_page_view wording (visitor; the ua user-agent string); clarified that disable() still validates before skipping the HTTP request and that both affect only the send functions; documented all response models and exception classes; added a package module docstring; and added runnable usage examples. Docstring-only — no code or behavior changes.



Fixed

validate_event_data no longer lets a whitespace-only event_name through (the check used and, so whitespace bypassed it; it now uses or).

title: Changelog
text:
[0.6.25] - 2026-06-07

Added

distinct_id support in new_event, new_page_view, and new_revenue_event payloads (sync and async), sent to Umami as payload field id
Umami Cloud API-key authentication via set_cloud_api_key(key, region=None) and clear_cloud_api_key(). In Cloud mode, data/management calls route to https://api.umami.is/v1[/region] with an x-umami-api-key header, and events are sent to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send — no set_url_base() or login() required. Existing self-hosted (login() + token) usage is byte-for-byte unchanged. Added urls.me for Cloud key validation in verify_token/verify_token_async. In Cloud mode, heartbeat() / heartbeat_async() check liveness via the authenticated /me endpoint (Cloud has no /api/heartbeat), and login() / login_async() raise OperationNotAllowedError to fail fast (the API key is the credential — there is no username/password login on Cloud).



Changed

validate_state error messages now mention set_cloud_api_key() alongside set_url_base() / login(). Same exception type (OperationNotAllowedError) and trigger conditions; text only.
Response models are more tolerant of variant/partial responses: WebsiteStats.comparison and Website.user are now optional, and Website accepts createUser (returned by team-website listings, where userId is null). Successful responses today are unaffected.
Internal: expanded the unit test suite (now 128 tests) following a suite review — added behavioral coverage for set_url_base validation, the validate_state guards, the login/login_async happy path and response-model deserialization (LoginResponse, WebsitesResponse), websites/websites_async, the disable() no-op (asserting no HTTP request is made), ip_address payload inclusion/omission, explicit-arg-overrides-defaults precedence, heartbeat_async self-hosted, and the verify_token/heartbeat failure branches. Added a sync/async parity harness and consolidated the per-file HTTP mock builders into a shared tests/_mocks.py (net ~210 fewer lines). No production behavior changed.



Fixed

website_stats_async() sent its date range as snake_case start_at/end_at query params, which the Umami API ignores — it silently returned all-time stats regardless of the requested window. Now sends camelCase startAt/endAt, matching the sync website_stats(). (#18)
active_users() and active_users_async() read the active-visitor count from a non-existent x key, so they always returned 0. They now read Umami’s current visitors key (falling back to the legacy x key for compatibility). (#19)
website_stats() / website_stats_async() sent their url and host filters under the old query-param names, which Umami renamed on 2025-10-07 (url → path, host → hostname) — so filtering stats by URL or hostname was a silent no-op. The public url/host keyword arguments are unchanged; they now map to the current path/hostname wire names. (#20)
heartbeat() / heartbeat_async() issued a POST to /api/heartbeat, which current Umami answers with 405 Method Not Allowed; the broad exception handler swallowed the error so the call always returned False even against a healthy server. They now issue a GET (the endpoint returns {"ok": true}).
new_event() and new_revenue_event() (sync) defaulted url to '/event-api-endpoint' while their async twins used '/'. All four now default to '/', so the sync/async twins agree and no placeholder path appears in dashboards.

Core Features

➕ Add a custom event to your Umami analytics dashboard.
💰 Track revenue with dedicated revenue event support.
📄 Add a page view to your Umami analytics dashboard.
🆔 Attach a per-user distinct_id to events, page views, and revenue (sent as the Umami payload id).

👥 Get active users count for real-time monitoring.

title: Umami Analytics Client for Python
text:
Development and Testing Support
🔧 Disable tracking in development: Use umami.disable() to disable all event and page view tracking without changing your code. Perfect for development and testing environments where you don’t want to pollute your analytics with test data.
import umami

# Configure as usual
umami.set_url_base("https://umami.hostedbyyouorthem.com")
umami.set_website_id('cc726914-8e68-4d1a-4be0-af4ca8933456')

umami.disable()

# These calls will return immediately without sending data to Umami
umami.new_event('test-event')  # No HTTP request made
umami.new_page_view('Test Page', '/test')  # No HTTP request made

umami.enable()

✅ No HTTP requests are made to your Umami server by new_event(), new_page_view(), or new_revenue_event()
✅ API calls still validate parameters (helps catch configuration issues)
✅ All other functions work normally and still contact the server (login, websites, stats, heartbeat, etc.)

title: Umami Analytics Client for Python
text:
Usage

import umami

umami.set_url_base("https://umami.hostedbyyouorthem.com")

# Auth is NOT required to send events, but is for other features.
login = umami.login(username, password)

# Skip the need to pass the target website in subsequent calls.
umami.set_website_id('cc726914-8e68-4d1a-4be0-af4ca8933456')
umami.set_hostname('somedomain.com')

# Optional: Disable tracking for development/testing
# umami.disable()  # Uncomment to disable tracking

# List your websites
websites = umami.websites()

# Create a new event in the events section of the dashboards.
event_resp = umami.new_event(
    website_id='a7cd-5d1a-2b33', # Only send if overriding default above
    event_name='Umami-Test',
    title='Umami-Test', # Defaults to event_name if omitted.
    hostname='somedomain.com', # Only send if overriding default above.
    url='/users/actions',
    custom_data={'client': 'umami-tester-v1'},
    distinct_id='user-123',  # OPTIONAL: stable per-user id, sent as payload id
    referrer='https://some_url')

# Create a new page view in the pages section of the dashboards.
page_view_resp = umami.new_page_view(
    website_id='a7cd-5d1a-2b33', # Only send if overriding default above
    page_title='Umami-Test', # Required: the page title to record.
    hostname='somedomain.com', # Only send if overriding default above.
    url='/users/actions',
    distinct_id='user-123',  # OPTIONAL: stable per-user id, sent as payload id
    referrer='https://some_url')

# Track revenue for a transaction
revenue_resp = umami.new_revenue_event(
    revenue=19.99,  # Monetary amount (required)
    currency='USD',  # ISO 4217 currency code, defaults to 'USD'
    event_name='checkout-cart',  # Defaults to 'revenue' if omitted
    url='/checkout',
    distinct_id='user-123',  # OPTIONAL: stable per-user id, sent as payload id
    custom_data={'product': 'widget', 'quantity': 2})

# Get website statistics for a date range
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

end_date = datetime.now()
start_date = end_date - timedelta(days=7)  # Last 7 days

stats = umami.website_stats(
    start_at=start_date,
    end_at=end_date,
    website_id='a7cd-5d1a-2b33'  # Only send if overriding default above
)
print(f"Page views: {stats.pageviews}")
print(f"Unique visitors: {stats.visitors}")
print(f"Bounces: {stats.bounces}")

# Get current active users count
active_count = umami.active_users(
    website_id='a7cd-5d1a-2b33'  # Only send if overriding default above
)
print(f"Currently active users: {active_count}")

# Check if Umami server is accessible
server_ok = umami.heartbeat()
print(f"Umami server is {'accessible' if server_ok else 'not accessible'}")

# Call after logging in to make sure the auth token is still valid.
umami.verify_token()
This code listing is very-very high fidelity pseudo code. If you want an actually executable example, see the example client in the repo. Sending events and Querying stats explain each call, and Troubleshooting covers what to do when a call raises or an event does not show up.

title: Umami Analytics Client for Python
text:
Umami Cloud
Using Umami Cloud instead of a self-hosted instance? Authenticate with an API key rather than login(). Create one in Umami Cloud under Settings → API keys.
In Cloud mode you do not call set_url_base() or login() — set_cloud_api_key() takes care of both the host routing and the authentication header for you:
import umami
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Authenticate with your Cloud API key. region is optional ('us' or 'eu');
# omit it to use the region of the account that owns the key.
umami.set_cloud_api_key("your-cloud-api-key", region="eu")
umami.set_website_id("your-website-id")

# Data/management calls go to https://api.umami.is/v1[/region]/...
# and send the x-umami-api-key header automatically.
active_count = umami.active_users()

end = datetime.now()
stats = umami.website_stats(start_at=end - timedelta(days=7), end_at=end)
print(f"Visitors (last 7 days): {stats.visitors}")

# Events are sent to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send automatically.
umami.new_event(event_name="purchase", url="/checkout", hostname="example.com")

# Return to self-hosted / token behavior at any time:
# umami.clear_cloud_api_key()

Routing is handled for you: data and management calls go to https://api.umami.is/v1 (authenticated with the x-umami-api-key header), while events are sent to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send. Umami documents a Cloud rate limit of 50 calls / 15 seconds per API key; the library does not throttle or retry.

The self-hosted (login()) usage shown above is unchanged — Cloud mode is simply a labeled alternative, and existing code keeps working exactly as before. The two modes are exclusive: login() raises OperationNotAllowedError while a Cloud key is set, and clear_cloud_api_key() switches back. Details in Authentication.

Disable event and page view tracking.

Source


disable()


When disabled, the send functions new_event(), new_revenue_event(), and new_page_view() still validate their arguments but then return without making any HTTP request to Umami. This is useful for development and testing environments.

title: errors.OperationNotAllowedError
text:
Raised when the SDK is missing required state for an operation.


Usage
Source


errors.OperationNotAllowedError()


A subclass of ValidationError. It signals that prerequisite configuration has not been completed, for example calling an operation before set_url_base() in self-hosted mode, querying data before login(), or calling login() while a Cloud API key is configured (login() is not used in Cloud mode).
Resolve it by calling the appropriate setup function first: set_url_base() and login() for self-hosted mode, or set_cloud_api_key() for Umami Cloud.


Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
try:
    umami.websites()  # no login() yet
except umami.errors.OperationNotAllowedError:
    umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
    sites = umami.websites()

title: heartbeat()
text:
Check whether the configured Umami server is reachable and healthy.


Usage
Source


heartbeat()


In self-hosted mode this issues a GET to {url_base}/api/heartbeat. In Cloud mode (after set_cloud_api_key()), Umami Cloud has no /api/heartbeat endpoint, so this performs an authenticated GET on the /me endpoint as a liveness check instead.
Requires set_url_base() (self-hosted) or set_cloud_api_key() (Cloud) to have been called first; login() is not required. This function never raises: any failure (missing configuration, connection error, or a non-2xx response) is caught and reported as False.


Returns


 bool

True if the server is reachable and responded successfully; False on
any error, including when no url_base or Cloud API key has been
configured.





Example
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
if not umami.heartbeat():
    print('Umami is unavailable')

title: Authentication
text: There are two ways to authenticate, and you use exactly one of them at a time. Self-hosted instances take a username and password and return a token. Umami Cloud takes an API key. The package routes requests and sets headers differently in each mode, so the choice matters even though the rest of your code stays the same.

title: Authentication
text:
Tokens expire
Umami login tokens are temporary. A long-running process should expect a query call to start failing with a 401 at some point. verify_token() checks the stored token against the server and never raises:
if not umami.verify_token():
    umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
verify_token(check_server=False) skips the network and only reports whether a credential is present, which is the same answer is_logged_in() gives.

title: FAQ
text:
Short answers to the questions that come up most. Each one links to the guide page with the full explanation.

Do I need to log in to send events?
No. new_event(), new_page_view(), and new_revenue_event() only need set_url_base() (or a Cloud key), a website id, and a hostname. Login is required for websites(), website_stats(), active_users(), and verify_token(). See Authentication.


Why is the package called umami-analytics but imported as umami?
umami-analytics is the name on PyPI. umami is the import name. A different, unrelated project owns the umami name on PyPI, so pip install umami installs the wrong thing.


Can the same code work for self-hosted and Umami Cloud?
Yes. Only the configuration step differs: set_url_base() plus login() for self-hosted, set_cloud_api_key() for Cloud. Every other call is identical, and the package routes requests and sets headers according to the mode. The two modes are exclusive, and clear_cloud_api_key() switches back.


My event call returned without an error but nothing is in the dashboard
The usual causes are tracking disabled (the call returned {}), a custom user agent that Umami’s bot filter rejected, the wrong website id, or looking at the wrong date range. Troubleshooting walks through them in order.


How do I keep tests from sending events?
Call umami.disable() in a test fixture. The send functions still validate their arguments and return {} without a request. Testing and CI has a fixture and shows how to mock the HTTP layer for the query functions.


Does it batch events or retry on failure?
No. Each call is one HTTP request with the httpx2 default five second timeout. Umami has an /api/batch endpoint, but the package does not wrap it. If you send events from a hot path, do it in a background task so a slow Umami server cannot slow your request.


Can I set the user agent on an event?
Only on page views, through the ua argument of new_page_view(). Custom events always use the package’s default browser user agent. Umami’s bot filter is the reason the default looks like Chrome.


What does distinct_id do?
It is sent as the payload field id and lets Umami attribute sessions and events to one logged-in user. Pass a str or int; blank values are dropped and other types raise ValidationError. See Sending events.


Is it thread safe?
The send and query functions only read module-global configuration, so calling them from many threads or tasks is fine. The setters write that state and are not synchronized, so configure once at startup. See How it works.


Which Python versions are supported?
Python 3.10 and newer. The runtime dependencies are httpx2 and pydantic.


Which parts of the Umami API are not covered?
Reports, sessions, event data, metrics and time series, realtime, teams, users, links, pixels, and share pages. How it works shows how to call them with the token or key you already have.


Where can an AI assistant read these docs?
The site publishes llms.txt (an index of the API reference) and llms-full.txt (every signature, docstring, and guide page), and an agent skill that teaches a coding agent the rules of the package. Every page is also available as Markdown by replacing .html with .md in its URL.

title: How it works
text:
This page describes what the package does on the wire, so you can reason about it when something is off and reach past it when you need an endpoint it does not wrap.

One module, global state
import umami gives you a module of functions, not a class. The public functions in umami are re-exports from umami.impl, which holds the configuration as module globals: the URL base, the login token, the default website id and hostname, the Cloud key and region, and the enabled flag. The set_* functions, login(), enable(), and disable() write those globals; everything else reads them.
That design has two consequences:

Configuration is per process. Two web workers each need their own set_url_base() and login() at startup.
The setters are not synchronized. Call them once at startup, before threads or an event loop start sending events. The send and query functions only read the globals, so concurrent calls after startup are fine.



Two modes, one code path
Every request resolves its URL and headers from the current mode.









Self-hosted
Umami Cloud




Selected by
set_url_base() and no Cloud key
set_cloud_api_key()


Events (/api/send)
{url_base}/api/send
https://cloud.umami.is/api/send


Queries
{url_base}/api/...
https://api.umami.is/v1[/region]/...


Query credential
Authorization: Bearer <token> from login()
x-umami-api-key: <key>


Event credential
the same Bearer header, which Umami ignores
none


verify_token()
POST /api/auth/verify
GET /me


heartbeat()
GET /api/heartbeat
GET /me with the key



In self-hosted mode the send functions include the Bearer header even when you never logged in, in which case its value is the string None. Umami’s ingestion endpoint does not read it, so this is harmless.


Two user agents
Umami drops ingestion requests whose user agent looks like a bot, because it is designed to receive data from browsers. The package therefore sends a desktop Chrome user agent on /api/send calls, and new_page_view() lets you replace it with the visitor’s real user agent through the ua argument. Query calls send an honest user agent of the form Umami-Client v1.0.0 / Python 3.14.10 / Darwin, available as umami.user_agent.
If you would rather Umami accepted any user agent, set DISABLE_BOT_CHECK=true in the Umami server’s environment.


Requests and responses
Each function makes exactly one HTTP request. The sync functions call httpx2.post() or httpx2.get() directly; the async functions open an httpx2.AsyncClient() for the call and close it afterwards. There is no connection pool, no retry, and no batching. Redirects are followed. The timeout is httpx2’s default of five seconds and is not configurable through the package.
Responses go through raise_for_status(), so any non-2xx status raises httpx2.HTTPStatusError with the response attached. The two exceptions are verify_token() and heartbeat(), which catch everything and return False, because they exist to answer a yes or no question.
Successful query responses are parsed into Pydantic models from umami.models. websites() unwraps Umami’s paged {"data": [...]} envelope and returns the list. website_stats() returns WebsiteStats. active_users() reads the visitors key and returns an int. Send functions return the response body as a plain dict.


Sync and async parity
Each _async twin builds the same payload, sends the same headers, hits the same URL, and returns the same value as its sync counterpart. The package’s test suite drives both and compares the request bodies, so a difference between the two is a test failure. The configuration functions are sync only because they do no I/O.


Dates and filters
website_stats() converts start_at and end_at to epoch milliseconds with datetime.timestamp(), which interprets naive datetimes in the local timezone. The filter keywords url and host are sent as path and hostname, the names Umami adopted in October 2025. The other filters are sent under their own names, and None values are omitted.


Beyond the wrapped endpoints
The package covers configuration, authentication, sending, listing websites, summary stats, and active users. For reports, sessions, event data, metrics, time series, realtime, teams, users, or anything else in the Umami API, make the call yourself with the credential you already have:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import httpx2 as httpx
import umami

base = 'https://umami.example.com'
umami.set_url_base(base)
login = umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')

end = datetime.now()
start = end - timedelta(days=7)
resp = httpx.get(
    f'{base}/api/websites/{website_id}/metrics',
    params={'startAt': int(start.timestamp() * 1000), 'endAt': int(end.timestamp() * 1000), 'type': 'url'},
    headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {login.token}'},
)
resp.raise_for_status()
top_pages = resp.json()
On Cloud, use https://api.umami.is/v1 as the base, drop the /api prefix from each path, and send {'x-umami-api-key': key} instead of the Bearer header.
Two conventions trip people up when calling the API directly. The GET stats, sessions, events, and revenue endpoints take startAt and endAt as Unix milliseconds in the query string. The POST /api/reports/* endpoints take startDate and endDate as ISO 8601 strings inside a parameters object in the body. The package hides the first convention for you; it does not touch the second.

title: Querying stats
text: Three functions read data out of Umami. All of them require a login token or a Cloud API key, and all of them raise httpx2.HTTPStatusError on a non-2xx response. Each has an _async twin.

title: Querying stats
text:
Dates
start_at and end_at are datetime objects. The package converts them to epoch milliseconds with timestamp(), which means a naive datetime is interpreted in the local timezone of the process. Pass timezone-aware datetimes if the server and your process run in different zones.

title: Querying stats
text:
Filters
Every optional keyword narrows the stats to matching traffic:
stats = umami.website_stats(start_at=start, end_at=end, url='/pricing', country='US', device='Mobile')
The filters are url, referrer, title, query, event, host, os, browser, device, country, region, and city. Two of them are renamed on the wire: url is sent as path and host is sent as hostname, which is what current Umami expects. Filters you leave as None are not sent.

title: Testing and CI
text:
Analytics calls in application code are a problem for test suites. Every test run would record fake purchases and page views against your real website, and a test environment without network access would fail on the first event. The package gives you two tools for this: a module-level switch that turns sending off, and a single HTTP boundary that is easy to mock.

Turn sending off with disable()
umami.disable() makes new_event(), new_page_view(), and new_revenue_event() (and their async twins) validate their arguments and then return {} without making a request. umami.enable() turns sending back on, and enabled is the default.
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')
umami.disable()

umami.new_event(event_name='signup')  # returns {} and sends nothing
Two details matter:

Validation still runs. A blank event name or a missing website id still raises ValidationError, so tests catch configuration mistakes without touching the network.
Only the send functions are affected. login(), websites(), website_stats(), active_users(), verify_token(), and heartbeat() always make their request. Mock those if a test reaches them.

The simplest production pattern is to decide at startup:
import os
import umami

umami.set_url_base(os.environ['UMAMI_URL'])
umami.set_website_id(os.environ['UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID'])
umami.set_hostname('example.com')

if os.environ.get('APP_ENV') != 'production':
    umami.disable()
The variable names are yours. The package reads no environment variables itself.


A pytest fixture
Because the configuration is module-global, one test can leak state into the next. An autouse fixture that resets everything keeps tests independent:
# conftest.py
import pytest
import umami


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _umami_offline():
    umami.set_url_base('https://umami.test')
    umami.set_website_id('test-website-id')
    umami.set_hostname('test.example')
    umami.clear_cloud_api_key()
    umami.disable()
    yield
With this in place, application code can call umami.new_event() freely and nothing leaves the test process.


Mock the HTTP boundary
When a test needs to assert what would have been sent, or needs a query function to return data, patch httpx2 where the package uses it. The package does import httpx2 as httpx inside umami.impl and calls httpx.post() and httpx.get() for the sync functions and httpx.AsyncClient() for the async ones. This is how the package’s own test suite works.
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import umami


def test_purchase_sends_revenue():
    umami.enable()
    response = MagicMock()
    response.json.return_value = {'cache': 'abc'}
    with patch('umami.impl.httpx.post', return_value=response) as post:
        umami.new_revenue_event(revenue=19.99, event_name='purchase', url='/checkout')

    body = post.call_args.kwargs['json']
    assert body['payload']['name'] == 'purchase'
    assert body['payload']['data'] == {'revenue': 19.99, 'currency': 'USD'}
For the async twins, patch umami.impl.httpx.AsyncClient with an object that works as an async context manager:
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

import umami


async def test_async_event():
    umami.enable()
    response = MagicMock()
    response.json.return_value = {}
    client = AsyncMock()
    client.__aenter__ = AsyncMock(return_value=client)
    client.__aexit__ = AsyncMock(return_value=False)
    client.post = AsyncMock(return_value=response)

    with patch('umami.impl.httpx.AsyncClient', return_value=client):
        await umami.new_event_async(event_name='signup')

    assert client.post.call_args.kwargs['json']['payload']['name'] == 'signup'
Async tests need pytest-asyncio. Setting asyncio_mode = "auto" in your pytest configuration removes the need for a marker on each test.
To test a query function, return the shape Umami returns. websites() expects {'data': [...], 'count': n, 'page': 1, 'pageSize': 10}, website_stats() expects the five integer fields pageviews, visitors, visits, bounces, and totaltime, and active_users() expects {'visitors': n}.


Continuous integration
Nothing in the package needs network access when tracking is disabled, so the fixture above is enough for CI. If your pipeline builds a container that runs the real application, make sure the environment variable that selects disable() is set in the test stage and unset in production. A forgotten disable() in production is silent: every call returns {} and no events arrive, which looks the same as a broken server. The Troubleshooting page lists this as the first thing to check.
